cases.exposure_context_quote: Here, we present a report of six cases of attempted suicide poisoning with pretilachlor herbicide and related organophosphorus toxicity symptoms.
cases.agent_quote: All the above patients confirmed to have ingested pretilachlor 50% emulsified concentrate (EC).
cases.circumstance: Attempted suicidal ingestion of pretilachlor herbicide

symptoms.finding: nausea, vomiting, salivation, lacrimation, abdominal cramps (series-level)
symptoms.quote: Later, the early symptoms of nausea, vomiting, salivation, lacrimation, and abdominal cramps disappeared.

symptoms.finding: nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, tachycardia; no fever, bradycardia, miosis, or hypotension (series-level)
symptoms.quote: In our instances, patients commonly present with symptoms of nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and tachycardia. Signs like fever, bradycardia, miosis, and hypotension were not present in any patients.

cases.time_to_care: All presented within 3 h of ingestion

labs.name: serum acetylcholinesterase
labs.quote: In all our patients, the enzyme level came out to be normal, which was a major hint to finally differentiate between the two poisonings.

labs.name: blood counts, glucose, LFT, RFT, electrolytes
labs.quote: In all the patients serial blood tests were performed including total blood counts, random blood glucose, liver and renal function tests, the reports of which turned out to be within normal ranges.

treatment.name: gastric lavage (all presented within 3 h)
treatment.quote: Upon presentation they were all subjected to gastric lavage as they all presented within 3 h of time frame.

treatment.name: IV fluids, antiemetics, prophylactic antibiotics, NPO, proton pump inhibitors
treatment.quote: The vital signs were stable and were carefully monitored while being managed with supportive measures such as intravenous fluids, antiemetics and prophylactic antibiotics.

cases.outcome: discharged after 3 days of hospital admission, clinically stable; no symptoms at one-week follow-up
cases.outcome_quote: They were discharged after 3 days of hospital admission as all of them were clinically stable. On follow-up after one week, no clinical signs and symptoms were observed.
